This receptor, in turn, is a target of doxorubicin, implying a potential regulatory role in the cellular response to the drug. The indirect pathway highlights a possible mechanism where doxorubicin influences the activity of a receptor that ultimately affects the function of the Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B3. This suggests that the transporter may be involved in the cellular response to Racotumomab, which is itself a target of doxorubicin. The integration of these relationships underscores a complex, multi-step interaction that may underlie the drug's biological effects.
